briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate change expert spokesperson briefing on August 9, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Global Impacts
sections.content: Today, we encountered voices defining the era of climate crisis as a 'great war for survival' [3, 14]. Europe's power grid is facing a complex climate change backlash, including heatwaves, droughts, and solar eclipses [7], while Japanese farmers are suffering economic blows such as decreased income and increased production costs due to heatwaves [11]. Domestically, 'meteorological droughts' have occurred in 48 locations, including Daegu and Busan, and with low rainfall expected in September, the southern Gyeongbuk and Gyeongnam regions are experiencing a 'caution' level drought [13, 15, 33, 41]. Heatwaves pose an even greater disaster for vulnerable populations [32, 35], and the rising water temperature of the Han River has raised the need to strengthen the response system for taste and odor-causing substances [39]. Internationally, the likelihood of wildfires in Canada has doubled due to climate change [48], and a warning has been issued that the El Niño phenomenon, expected to persist until early next spring, could lead to a wet winter and increased flood risk in the western and southeastern United States [51].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Adaptation Efforts and Food Security
sections.content: Despite the threats of climate change, various adaptation efforts are underway domestically. Sangju City is promoting a pilot project to diversify apple varieties, such as 'Golden Ball,' in response to climate change, thereby enhancing cultivation stability [4, 5, 6, 9, 10]. Various local governments, including Haenam County, are making all-out efforts to secure national funding for maintaining pleasant urban environments and responding to climate change [1, 2]. Nonghyup is providing 300 billion won in emergency funds to disaster-stricken farms affected by heatwaves and droughts [38]. Furthermore, field-oriented support, such as the introduction of 'mobile shelters' for farmers working in the heat, is also being implemented [40].

sections.title: 🌱 Carbon Neutrality Goals and Accelerated Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: The Republic of Korea recognizes carbon neutrality as an essential task for the future and is accelerating its transition to renewable energy [20]. Haenam County is establishing a carbon-neutral forest model by creating a specialized forest on Mandaesan Mountain [16, 17], and 680.7 billion won has been invested in saline reclaimed land to begin the construction of a 400 MW renewable energy complex [27]. Jeju Island is exploring innovative solutions, such as building a 40 MW 'Green Data Center' using surplus renewable energy and supporting vulnerable households with electricity bills for cooling costs from wind power development profits [26, 29]. Pohang City is enhancing environmental awareness among future generations by hosting a 'Carbon-Neutral Electric Vehicle' summer camp utilizing AI and coding [21, 22, 24], and Yanggu County has also begun accepting applications for electric vehicle dissemination [23]. Concurrently, Policy Committee Chairperson Han Jeoung-ae is discussing climate change response policies, including reviewing the easing of the progressive electricity tariff system during heatwave periods [31].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges in Carbon Neutrality Implementation and Environmental Issues
sections.content: The journey towards carbon neutrality still presents challenges that need to be addressed. Amazon, which declared carbon neutrality, sparked controversy by investing in a large gas-fired power plant [18], and the rising price of greenhouse gas emission allowances, which has tripled, is increasing Jeonju City's financial burden [25]. This indicates the economic and policy difficulties that companies and local governments may face during the carbon neutrality implementation process. Furthermore, the argument that 'to prevent war, we must invest in climate solutions, not military spending' raises important questions about the priorities of climate crisis response [8]. Moreover, research indicating that microplastic contamination is continuously found during food waste treatment and can leach into agricultural land demonstrates the need for a thorough review of the environmental sustainability of circular economy models [50].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the challenges faced both domestically and internationally amidst the deepening global climate crisis, while also shedding light on the multifaceted efforts to overcome these challenges and the tasks that lie ahead. It is imperative to understand the complexities of the era of climate crisis and to continue wise responses for a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
